key_insight: Reducing memory to delayed feedback enables optimistic constrained online learning with guarantees that adapt to environment changes and prediction accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports stateful online learning and non-stochastic control under time-varying budget constraints, using predictions without requiring them to be reliable.
method: Reduce memory effects to delay and treat state-dependent gradients as delayed feedback.
Incorporate untrusted predictions into an optimistic constrained online optimization algorithm.
Adapt dynamic regret and cumulative constraint violation bounds to path length and prediction accuracy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees, not empirical evaluation: perfect predictions yield O(1) regret, with cumulative constraint violation O(√T) for unknown path length or O(log T) when path length is known or online observable.
watch_item: The strongest constraint-violation guarantee requires known or online-observable path length, which may be unavailable in deployment.
paper_title: Dynamic Optimistic Constrained OCO with Memory via Delay Equivalence
